item.name: AI Maturity Model
item.description: A methodology and qualitative benchmarking framework for assessing and guiding an organization's AI adoption maturity.
item.grounding_span: The MITRE AI Maturity Model (AI MM) can be viewed as a methodology to provide guidance and recommendations for enabling a foundation for successful AI implementations across an organization.

item.name: AI Adoption
item.description: Organizations committing to investing in, employing, and deriving continued value from AI capabilities.
item.grounding_span: Pursuit by organizations and/or individuals to commit to investing in, employing, and deriving continued value from AI capabilities.

item.name: AI Maturity
item.description: An organization's progress in becoming adept at incorporating AI technologies and best practices.
item.grounding_span: measure an organization’s progress in AI maturity as it becomes increasingly adept at incorporating AI technologies and best practices into its work environment

item.name: Artificial Intelligence
item.description: The ability of machines to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.
item.grounding_span: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are advanced technologies whose application can elevate and enhance the value proposition associated with business process improvements and strategic goals.

item.name: Machine Learning
item.description: Advanced technology applied alongside AI; introduces new considerations such as adversarial machine learning.
item.grounding_span: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are advanced technologies

item.name: Maturity Model
item.description: A tool that defines objective evaluation criteria to help organizations assess effectiveness and identify next steps to improve performance.
item.grounding_span: Maturity models are tools that define objective evaluation criteria to help organizations assess their current effectiveness and identify next steps to improve performance.

item.name: Pillars
item.description: Structured groups of related functional areas (dimensions) important to successful AI adoption.
item.grounding_span: Structured group of related functional areas (dimensions) that are important factors in successful AI adoption.

item.name: Dimensions
item.description: Functional and measurable features foundational to successful AI adoption maturity.
item.grounding_span: Functional and measurable features that are foundational to successful AI adoption and that describe specific focus areas critical to AI adoption maturity.

item.name: Supporting Evidence
item.description: Sources of information used to determine whether an organization has satisfied key aspects of a pillar's maturity level.
item.grounding_span: Evidence used to determine a level of maturity is the final component of the model.

item.name: Data Literacy
item.description: Organizational competency in data considered critical to AI adoption maturity and correlated with business value.
item.grounding_span: It is also necessary for establishing a data-literate organization, which is critical to AI adoption maturity.

item.name: Human-Machine Mutual Learning
item.description: Mutual learning and feedback between humans and machines that generates value from AI.
item.grounding_span: The study highlights the often-underestimated role of mutual learning between humans and machines in generating value from AI.

item.name: Adversarial Machine Learning
item.description: A new type of vulnerability introduced by AI that conventional software security policies may ignore.
item.grounding_span: it might ignore new types of vulnerabilities introduced by AI, such as adversarial machine learning

item.name: Federally Funded Research and Development Center
item.description: A special class of research centers providing Federal agencies R&D capabilities not met by the Federal government or private industry.
item.grounding_span: Federally funded research and development centers (FFRDCs) are a special class of research centers dedicated to providing Federal agencies with research and development capabilities that cannot be met by the Federal government or private industries.

item.name: Trustworthiness
item.description: Ability of an AI solution to produce human confidence through accuracy, reliability, explainability, security, and safety.
item.grounding_span: Ability of an AI solution to produce human confidence throughout its performance,  through demonstrated accuracy, reliability, explainability, security, and safety.

item.name: Ethical, Equitable, and Responsible Use
item.description: Pillar establishing expectations, requirements, and governance to mitigate risks of negative or unintended consequences of AI initiatives.
item.grounding_span: Establish expectations, requirements, and governance to mitigate risks of negative or unintended consequences of AI initiatives.

item.name: Strategy and Resources
item.description: Pillar ensuring availability of AI solution strategic plans, governance model, and needed resources.
item.grounding_span: To ensure the availability of AI solution strategic plans governance model and needed resources.

item.name: Organization
item.description: Pillar ensuring enterprise-level embrace of AI through culture, roles and responsibilities, and workforce development.
item.grounding_span: Ensure AI that is embraced at an enterprise level includes culture, roles and responsibilities, and workforce development to enable effective AI solutions.

item.name: Technology Enablers
item.description: Pillar ensuring establishment of technology enablers including innovation, testing, and infrastructure to produce AI solutions.
item.grounding_span: Ensure the establishment of technology enablers, including innovation, testing, and infrastructure to produce AI solutions.

item.name: Data
item.description: Pillar ensuring AI initiatives have the needed data for effective and successful implementation.
item.grounding_span: Ensure that AI initiatives have the needed data for effective and successful implementation.

item.name: Performance and Application
item.description: Pillar ensuring effective and efficient development, deployment, operation, and maintenance of AI-enabled capabilities.
item.grounding_span: Ensure the effective and efficient development, deployment, operation, and maintenance of AI-enabled capabilities.

item.name: Responsible, Governable, and Contestable
item.description: Oversight and governance to enforce compliance of AI development and outcomes, with accountability and the ability to contest.
item.grounding_span: Oversight and governance are in place to enforce regulatory and enterprise-wide compliance of AI system development and outcomes, including timely processes for accountability and to allow challenges to use and outputs.

item.name: Transparency
item.description: AI systems decisions, outputs, and outcomes are explainable, justifiable, and transparent.
item.grounding_span: AI systems decisions, outputs, and outcomes are explainable, justifiable, and transparent to users and those impacted by them.

item.name: Human-Centric, Fair, and Equitable
item.description: AI systems designed to accommodate human rights, diversity, and well-being while avoiding bias and unfair discrimination.
item.grounding_span: AI systems are designed to accommodate human rights, diversity, and well-being through use of deliberate steps to avoid bias and unfair and/or unintended discrimination or inequitable consequences.

item.name: AI Strategic Plan
item.description: Formal documents/artifacts supporting a plan for achieving defined AI mission, vision, policies, and standards.
item.grounding_span: Formal documents/artifacts that support a plan for achieving defined AI mission, vision, policies, and standards.

item.name: Partnerships
item.description: AI partnerships among government, private enterprise, academia, and FFRDCs to ensure diverse perspectives and build responsible AI capabilities.
item.grounding_span: AI partnerships between government, private enterprises, academic institutions, and/or federally funded research and development centers (FFRDCs) are available to collaborate with

item.name: Governance
item.description: AI governance structures, processes, policies, and audits promoting conformance with ethics, regulations, and policies.
item.grounding_span: AI governance structures, standardized processes, policies, and audits are available to promote conformance with the entity’s ethics, regulations, and policies.

item.name: Culture
item.description: Organizational norms and values supporting an adaptive, risk-tolerant culture ready to accept AI-driven change.
item.grounding_span: The organizational norms and values support an adaptive and risk-tolerant culture that is ready to accept the types of changes that AI might entail.

item.name: Organizational Structure
item.description: AI structures, roles, and processes defined, documented, and executed within the enterprise.
item.grounding_span: AI structures, roles, and processes are defined, documented, and executed within the enterprise.

item.name: Workforce Development
item.description: Processes for diverse AI teams' training, recruitment, and career impact awareness to develop and reshape an AI workforce.
item.grounding_span: Processes are in place for diverse AI teams’ training, recruitment, and career impact awareness to develop and reshape an AI organizational workforce.

item.name: AI Innovation
item.description: Process integrating research, systems engineering, and human-machine design principles to embed AI into business operations.
item.grounding_span: Process whereby research, systems engineering, and human-machine design principles and best practices integrate AI into business operations.

item.name: Test and Evaluation
item.description: AI-specific T&E standards ensuring solution requirements are verified and validated.
item.grounding_span: AI-specific T&E standards ensure that solution requirements are verified and validated to meet all identified requirements.

item.name: AI Platforms
item.description: Enabling architecture, standards, networking, hardware, and software tools supporting AI solution development and operation.
item.grounding_span: A defined set of enabling architecture, standards, computer networking, hardware, and software tools are designed to support development, integration, and operation of AI solutions.

item.name: Data Architecture
item.description: Process of ingesting, storing, organizing, and maintaining data created and collected by an organization, including lexicon and ontology.
item.grounding_span: Process of ingesting, storing, organizing, and maintaining the data created and collected by an organization, including the lexicon and ontology.

item.name: Security and Privacy
item.description: Protection of privacy and data security rights for AI, controlling safety, specificity, and exchange of personal digital information.
item.grounding_span: Protection of privacy rights and data security rights for AI is embedded and upheld by individuals designing, using, and overseeing AI systems to control the safety, specificity, and exchange of personal digital information.

item.name: AI Data Governance
item.description: Managing AI data performance and compliance to guard against data bias and ensure availability, usability, and integrity.
item.grounding_span: Process of managing AI data performance and compliance to guard against data bias and ensure availability, usability, and integrity of data in AI systems.

item.name: Accessibility
item.description: A systematic approach to managing trusted and secure data sharing internally and externally.
item.grounding_span: A systematic approach and structure to address the challenges, legal agreements, and requirements needed for managing trusted and secure data sharing both internally and externally.

item.name: Usage and Adoption
item.description: Identifying and documenting AI business use cases and integrating solutions into workflows to realize strategic outcomes.
item.grounding_span: Identification and documentation of AI business use cases and the application of integrated solutions and processes into workflows result in realized strategic outcomes.

item.name: Solution Monitoring
item.description: Tools and processes monitoring deployed AI solutions for changes in performance, fairness, security, or user trust over time.
item.grounding_span: A combination of tools and processes that monitor deployed AI solutions to detect any changes in performance, fairness, security, or user trust over time.

item.name: Robust and Reliable
item.description: AI systems well defined, designed, and tested across the lifecycle to execute per intended purpose and meet quality parameters.
item.grounding_span: AI systems are well defined, designed, and tested across the entire lifecycle—including operations—to ensure that they execute in accordance with intended purpose, avoid failures and malfunctions, and meet required quality parameters.

item.name: User Trust
item.description: Repeatability, traceability, transparency, and explainability supported by due diligence to calibrate appropriate levels of trust.
item.grounding_span: Repeatability, traceability, transparency, and explainability are supported by due diligence processes, standards, and techniques to design, measure, and calibrate AI solutions to promote appropriate levels of trust.

item.name: Level 1: Initial
item.description: Nascent AI efforts lacking senior leadership, governance, strategy, and direction; no AI sponsor or champion designated.
item.grounding_span: Nascent AI efforts lack senior management leadership, governance, strategy, and direction for key areas necessary for adoption.

item.name: Level 2: Engaged
item.description: A more organized approach to AI with champions, team building, governance, and strategies; solutions still decentralized.
item.grounding_span: There is a more organized approach to AI with emphasis on establishing champions, team building, governance, and strategies for successful adoption.

item.name: Level 3: Defined
item.description: Approved enterprise-wide approaches, resources, and processes documented; governance, culture, strategies, and leadership in place.
item.grounding_span: Approved enterprise-wide approaches, resources, and processes are documented for AI projects, initiatives, and adoption efforts.

item.name: Level 4: Managed
item.description: AI initiatives follow policy, governance, and standards; outcomes and metrics collected, analyzed, and used to determine impact.
item.grounding_span: AI initiatives follow policy, governance, and technical standards. Outcomes and supporting metrics are collected, analyzed, and utilized to determine impact.

item.name: Level 5: Optimized
item.description: The enterprise produces high-level AI work by continually improving and innovating; silos broken down to integrate data and resources.
item.grounding_span: The enterprise produces high-level AI work by continually improving and innovating its AI projects.

item.verbatim_text: Pursuit by organizations and/or individuals to commit to investing in, employing, and deriving continued value from AI capabilities.
item.grounding_span: Pursuit by organizations and/or individuals to commit to investing in, employing, and deriving continued value from AI capabilities.

item.verbatim_text: Dedicated management of AI data performance and compliance to guard against data bias and ensure ethical and responsible use, availability, usability, integrity, privacy, and security of data in AI systems.
item.grounding_span: Dedicated management of AI data performance and compliance to guard against data bias and ensure ethical and responsible use, availability, usability, integrity, privacy, and security of data in AI systems.

item.verbatim_text: Careful and persistent use of requisite AI and machine learning (ML) tools and resources to achieve the best possible outcomes while mitigating risk.
item.grounding_span: Careful and persistent use of requisite AI and machine learning (ML) tools and resources to achieve the best possible outcomes while mitigating risk.

item.verbatim_text: Process whereby research, systems engineering, human-machine design principles, and best practices integrate AI into transformational, cutting-edge business applications.
item.grounding_span: Process whereby research, systems engineering, human-machine design principles, and best practices integrate AI into transformational, cutting-edge business applications.

item.verbatim_text: Defined set of hardware, software, networking tools, and services designed to support the development, adoption, use, and management of AI across an organization.
item.grounding_span: Defined set of hardware, software, networking tools, and services designed to support the development, adoption, use, and management of AI across an organization.

item.verbatim_text: Documented relationships between government, private enterprises, academic institutions, and FFRDCs to effect collaboration and increase AI capabilities and competencies.
item.grounding_span: Documented relationships between government, private enterprises, academic institutions, and FFRDCs to effect collaboration and increase AI capabilities and competencies.

item.verbatim_text: Defined levels of progress improvement (maturity) within AI adoption processes. As part of the AI Maturity Model, assessment levels include: Initial, Engaged, Defined, Managed, and Optimized.
item.grounding_span: Defined levels of progress improvement (maturity) within AI adoption processes. As part of the AI Maturity Model, assessment levels include: Initial, Engaged, Defined, Managed, and Optimized.

item.verbatim_text: Explainable AI is the extent to which the mechanics and performance of an AI system can be explained in human terms and clearly understood.
item.grounding_span: Explainable AI is the extent to which the mechanics and performance of an AI system can be explained in human terms and clearly understood.

item.verbatim_text: Conduct of ensuring and overseeing performance and compliance of AI policies, ethics, accountability to responsible use, technical standards, and change management practices in a fair manner.
item.grounding_span: Conduct of ensuring and overseeing performance and compliance of AI policies, ethics, accountability to responsible use, technical standards, and change management practices in a fair manner.

item.verbatim_text: A design approach for information technology systems that is characterized by humanistic values and observance of human welfare. When applied to AI, this approach emphasizes the importance of user needs and desires.
item.grounding_span: A design approach for information technology systems that is characterized by humanistic values and observance of human welfare. When applied to AI, this approach emphasizes the importance of user needs and desires.

item.name: AI Assessment Tool (AT)
item.method: Multiple-choice questionnaire — 20 questions, one per dimension, single answer per question generating a score and graphical visualization.
item.grounding_span: The AI AT consists of a series of multiple-choice questions—one for each dimension of the AI MM. There is only one answer that can be selected for each question, and the chosen response determines the level of maturity within that dimension.

item.text: AT question for Responsible, Governable, and Contestable — Level 1: No responsible use governance process is in place for accountability and to ensure regulatory and widespread compliance of AI solution outcomes, including data bias indicators and the ability to contest findings.
item.grounding_span: No responsible use governance process is in place for accountability and to ensure regulatory and widespread compliance of  AI solution outcomes, including data bias indicators and the ability to contest findings.

item.text: AT question for Transparency — Level 1: No standardized approaches exist that enable clear traceability for AI outputs/outcomes.
item.grounding_span: No standardized approaches exist that enable clear traceability for AI outputs/outcomes enabling transparency and the ability to explain and justify results.

item.text: AT question for Human-Centric, Fair, and Equitable — Level 1: No clear policies, standards, and approaches to ensure responsible use of AI.
item.grounding_span: No clear policies, standards, and approaches to ensure responsible use of AI through respect of human rights, diversity, well-being, fairness, and equitability.

item.text: AT question for AI Strategic Plan — Level 1: No enterprise-based AI mission/vision statement, policies, standards, leadership roles, or budget are present.
item.grounding_span: No enterprise-based AI mission/vision statement, policies, standards, leadership roles, or budget are present.

item.text: AT question for Partnerships — Level 1: No AI partnership(s) with industry, academia, or other agencies exist.
item.grounding_span: No AI partnership(s) with industry, academia, or other agencies exist.

item.text: AT question for Governance — Level 1: No AI governance structure, audits, processes, and standards are in place.
item.grounding_span: No AI governance structure, audits, processes, and standards are in place.

item.text: AT question for Culture — Level 1: The organizational entity has not absorbed norms that support widespread acceptance and use of AI.
item.grounding_span: AI projects may exist, but the organizational entity has not absorbed norms that support widespread acceptance and use of AI.

item.text: AT question for Workforce Development — Level 1: No solution or workforce plan is in place for AI workforce development.
item.grounding_span: No solution or workforce plan is in place for AI workforce development.

item.text: AT question for AI Platforms — Level 1: No AI-specific platform, processes, and tools are available.
item.grounding_span: No AI-specific platform, processes, and tools are available.

item.text: AT question for Data Architecture — Level 1: No common AI data architecture/framework is in place.
item.grounding_span: No common AI data architecture/framework is in place.

item.text: AT question for Security and Privacy — Level 1: No AI-specific privacy and data security rights, approaches, and standards are in place.
item.grounding_span: No AI-specific privacy and data security rights, approaches, and standards are in place for individual security, control, safety, and specificity in exchange for digital information.

item.text: AT question for AI Data Governance — Level 1: No AI data governance process or entity is in place.
item.grounding_span: No AI data governance process or entity is in place.

item.text: AT question for Accessibility — Level 1: No data-sharing service framework or agreement is in place.
item.grounding_span: No data-sharing service framework or agreement is in place.

item.text: AT question for Usage and Adoption — Level 1: No AI business use cases are identified or documented.
item.grounding_span: No AI business use cases are identified or documented. Needed skills, integrated solutions, and processes are not linked to workflows.

item.text: AT question for Robust and Reliable — Level 1: No AI-specific robustness and reliability standards/approaches are in place.
item.grounding_span: No AI-specific robustness and reliability standards/approaches are in place to ensure solutions meet quality requirements and intended use.

item.text: AT question for User Trust — Level 1: No systematic due diligence processes, techniques, and standards are in place to measure and calibrate user trust.
item.grounding_span: No systematic due diligence processes, techniques, and standards are in place to measure and calibrate user trust in AI systems.

item.name: Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Computational techniques that simulate human cognitive capabilities.
item.grounding_span: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the computational techniques that simulate human cognitive capabilities.

item.name: Narrow AI
item.description: Present-day AI that is task-specific rather than general.
item.grounding_span: All of the AI in place today is task-specific, or narrow AI.

item.name: Artificial General Intelligence
item.description: AI that achieves general human-level intelligence; not technically possible today.
item.grounding_span: This is known as Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) which, at this point, is not technically possible.

item.name: Machine Learning
item.description: Using algorithms that learn by extracting patterns from data.
item.grounding_span: Machine Learning (ML) refers to the field and practice of using algorithms that are able to “learn” by extracting patterns from a large body of data.

item.name: Supervised learning
item.description: ML using labeled datasets to classify data or predict outcomes.
item.grounding_span: Supervised learning uses labeled datasets to train algorithms to classify data or predict outcomes.

item.name: Unsupervised learning
item.description: ML using unlabeled data to discover patterns for clustering or association.
item.grounding_span: Unsupervised learning uses unlabeled data. From that data, it discovers patterns that help solve clustering or association problems.

item.name: Reinforcement learning
item.description: ML that learns by trial and error, reinforcing successful outcomes.
item.grounding_span: Reinforcement learning sequence of successful outcomes will be reinforced to develop the best recommendation for a given problem.

item.name: Data science
item.description: Cross-functional discipline producing data-driven insights and processes.
item.grounding_span: Data science is a broad field that covers a broad range of analytics and computer science techniques.

item.name: Deep learning
item.description: Computationally intensive ML often requiring GPU acceleration.
item.grounding_span: such as for Deep Learning and GPU acceleration.

item.name: Neural networks
item.description: Systems designed to think or act like a human.
item.grounding_span: including cognitive architectures and neural networks.

item.name: Clustering
item.description: Data mining technique grouping unlabeled data by similarity.
item.grounding_span: Clustering is a data mining technique which groups unlabeled data based on their similarities or differences.

item.name: Association
item.description: Discovering relationships between variables in a dataset.
item.grounding_span: Association is used to discover interesting relationships between variables in a dataset.

item.name: Dimensionality reduction
item.description: Reducing dimensions while maintaining meaningful properties.
item.grounding_span: Dimensionality reduction is used to reduce the number of dimensions while still maintaining meaningful properties close to the original data.

item.name: Predictive analytics
item.description: Anticipating results based on output variables.
item.grounding_span: Predictive analytics is used to provide deep insights into various data points and allows for the anticipation of results based on given output variables.

item.name: Computer vision
item.description: Visual perception tasks such as object recognition.
item.grounding_span: Computer vision: used for visual perception tasks such as object recognition.

item.name: Anomaly detection
item.description: Discovering atypical data points within a dataset.
item.grounding_span: Anomaly detection: used for going through large amounts of data and discovering atypical data points within a dataset.

item.name: Natural language processing
item.description: Processing language for tasks like translation.
item.grounding_span: and language translation using natural language processing

item.name: Human-machine teams
item.description: Pairing humans and machines each on best-suited tasks.
item.grounding_span: It is more appropriate to think in terms of human-machine teams where each does the tasks for which it is best-suited.

item.name: Bias in AI systems
item.description: Bias entering an AI system in many forms.
item.grounding_span: Bias can enter an AI system in many ways.

item.name: Data governance
item.description: Exercise of authority and control over data assets.
item.grounding_span: Data governance is the exercise of authority and control (planning, monitoring, and enforcement) over data assets.

item.name: Data lifecycle management
item.description: Managing the value of data throughout its lifecycle.
item.grounding_span: Data lifecycle management is the development, execution, and supervision of plans, policies, programs, and practices that deliver, control, protect, and enhance the value of data and information assets throughout their lifecycles

item.name: Metadata tagging
item.description: Standardizing metadata captured for new data sources.
item.grounding_span: One example of data lifecycle management is standardizing metadata captured for new data sources by populating a data card used to describe the data.

item.name: Chief Data Officer
item.description: Executive-branch role mandated by the Evidence Act.
item.grounding_span: requires every executive branch agency to establish a Chief Data Officer (CDO)

item.name: Integrated Product Team
item.description: Team responsible for implementing AI products, systems, and solutions.
item.grounding_span: The Integrated Product Team (IPT is responsible for implementing AI products, systems, and solutions.

item.name: Integrated Agency Team
item.description: Security, legal, and acquisition support for the IPT.
item.grounding_span: The value of an IAT is to support the IPT members who will actually develop and manage the day-to-day affairs

item.name: Central AI technical resource
item.description: Hub of AI expertise, tools, and infrastructure support.
item.grounding_span: A central AI technical resource–discussed below–will serve as a hub of AI expertise for program offices to seek the support they need.

item.name: AI practitioner
item.description: The people who do the AI work and need the tools.
item.grounding_span: The people doing the work are the AI practitioners who need the tools to do the work.

item.name: Responsible and trustworthy AI
item.description: AI encompassing accuracy, explainability, privacy, safety, bias mitigation.
item.grounding_span: responsibility includes: accuracy, explainability and interpretability, privacy, reliability, robustness, safety, security, the mitigation of harmful bias, and more as the field evolves.

item.name: Explainability and interpretability
item.description: Systems providing clear reasoning for outputs.
item.grounding_span: Designing systems that provide clear, understandable reasoning for their outputs.

item.name: Model drift
item.description: Performance change of a deployed model over time.
item.grounding_span: In production, models can “drift,” meaning that the performance will change over time.

item.name: Generalization
item.description: A model's ability to adapt to new, previously unseen data.
item.grounding_span: a process known as generalization, or the model’s ability to adapt properly to new, previously unseen data.

item.name: AI lifecycle
item.description: Iterative process from business problem to AI solution.
item.grounding_span: The AI lifecycle is the iterative process of moving from a business problem to an AI solution that solves that problem.

item.name: AI use case
item.description: A specific challenge or opportunity AI may solve.
item.grounding_span: A use case is a specific challenge or opportunity that AI may solve.

item.name: Buy or build
item.description: Decision on acquiring vs. developing AI capability.
item.grounding_span: Answering the “buy or build” question depends on the program office’s function and the nature of the commercial offering.

item.name: Test and Evaluation
item.description: Providing knowledge to manage risk in developing and sustaining systems.
item.grounding_span: The basic purpose of Test & Evaluation (T&E) is to provide knowledge to manage risk that’s involved in developing, producing, operating, and sustaining systems and capabilities.

item.name: Developmental Test and Evaluation
item.description: Verifies a system meets technical performance specifications.
item.grounding_span: First is developmental test and evaluation (DT&E), which verifies that a system meets technical performance specifications.

item.name: Operational Test and Evaluation
item.description: Testing under realistic operational conditions with the operator.
item.grounding_span: In time, operational test and evaluation (OT&E) follows.

item.name: Ethical T&E
item.description: Ensuring the system does only what it is supposed to.
item.grounding_span: Depending on the AI solution’s purpose, this step ensures the system does only what it’s supposed to do and doesn’t do what it’s not supposed to do.

item.name: Model T&E
item.description: Running the model on test data and scoring performance.
item.grounding_span: In this step, the model is run on the test data and its performance is scored based on metrics identified in the test planning process.

item.name: DevSecOps
item.description: Integrated practice of software development, IT operations, and security.
item.grounding_span: DevSecOps is the integrated practice of bringing together software development, IT operations, and the security team.

item.name: Infrastructure as Code
item.description: Bringing software-development discipline to infrastructure management.
item.grounding_span: Infrastructure as code (IaC) brings the repeatability, transparency, and testing of modern software development to the management of infrastructure such as networks, load balancers, virtual machines, Kubernetes clusters, and monitoring.

item.name: Cloud platform
item.description: Elastic storage and compute underpinning many AI tools.
item.grounding_span: Many AI tools and solutions are tied to a cloud platform.

item.name: AutoML
item.description: Tools automating model training and deployment.
item.grounding_span: AutoML tools—tools that automate many of the model training and deployment processes—are an emerging area of AI tool development.

item.name: PeopleOps
item.description: Recruit, develop, retain, and organize an AI-ready workforce.
item.grounding_span: Recruit, develop, retain, and organize an AI-ready workforce.

item.name: CloudOps
item.description: Provide and allocate storage, compute, and other cloud resources.
item.grounding_span: Provide and allocate storage, compute, and other resources in the cloud.

item.name: SecOps
item.description: Security best practices and protection of AI techniques from attacks.
item.grounding_span: SecOps unifies best practices in security for software development, system administration, data access, and protection of AI techniques from attacks.

item.name: DevOps
item.description: Securely moving software into production with CI/CD.
item.grounding_span: A mature AI organization must be able to securely move software into a production environment and provide continuous integration and delivery of software updates.

item.name: DataOps
item.description: Enabling data discovery, access, and use for AI development.
item.grounding_span: To deliver data to development teams, DataOps enables data discovery, access, and use for AI development.

item.name: MLOps
item.description: Selection, deployment, and maintenance of ML models in an AI system.
item.grounding_span: MLOps is the selection, application, interpretation, deployment, and maintenance of machine learning models within an AI-enabled system.

item.name: AIOps
item.description: AI capability development as systems engineering and product management.
item.grounding_span: AIOps support AI capability development as a discipline of systems engineering and product management.

item.name: Five Vs
item.description: Descriptive metadata dimensions for datasets.
item.grounding_span: metadata can be applied to datasets that detail information on the Five Vs

item.name: Statement of Objectives
item.description: Acquisition vehicle for uncertain solution paths.
item.grounding_span: Use a Statement of Objectives (SOO) when you are less certain of a solution’s path and want to consider innovative or unorthodox methods.

item.name: Performance Work Statement
item.description: Acquisition vehicle for clear specifications with measurable standards.
item.grounding_span: Consider using a Performance Work Statement (PWS) when you have clear specifications on what the product or service needs to do.

item.name: Commercial-off-the-shelf
item.description: Ready-made commercial products for some AI applications.
item.grounding_span: Some applications, such as voice recognition, can be deployed from commercial-of-the-shelf (COTS) products.

item.name: Organizational maturity areas
item.description: Capacity to embed AI capabilities across the organization.
item.grounding_span: Organizational maturity areas represent the capacity to embed AI capabilities across the organization.

item.name: Operational maturity areas
item.description: Organizational functions impacting implementation of AI capabilities.
item.grounding_span: Operational maturity areas represent organizational functions that impact the implementation of AI capabilities.

item.name: Initial / Ad Hoc
item.description: Process is unpredictable, poorly controlled, and unmanaged.
item.grounding_span: Process is unpredictable, poorly controlled, and unmanaged.

item.name: Repeatable
item.description: Documented, repeatable steps with consistent results.
item.grounding_span: Process is documented and steps are repeatable with consistent results. Often reactionary.

item.name: Defined
item.description: Documented, standardized processes improved over time.
item.grounding_span: Documented, standardized processes that are improved over time.

item.name: Managed
item.description: Activities measured with active, evidence-based management.
item.grounding_span: Activities are effectively measured, and meeting objectives are based on active management and evidence-based outcomes.

item.name: Optimized
item.description: Continuous performance improvement through innovation.
item.grounding_span: Continuous performance improvement of activities through incremental and innovative improvements.

item.name: Data analyst
item.description: Answers routine operational questions with data analysis.
item.grounding_span: focuses on answering routine operational questions using well-established data analysis techniques, including AI tools.

item.name: Data engineer
item.description: Builds data science/AI tools for reliability and scale.
item.grounding_span: focuses on carefully building and engineering data science and AI tools for reliability, accuracy, and scale.

item.name: Data scientist
item.description: Designs data science/AI models, tools, and techniques.
item.grounding_span: focuses on thoughtfully and rigorously designing data science/AI models, tools, and techniques.

item.name: Technical program manager
item.description: Manages software development teams building AI tools.
item.grounding_span: manages software development teams, including teams building AI tools and capabilities.

item.name: AI champion
item.description: Advocates for the AI solution's value.
item.grounding_span: Advocates for the AI solution’s value

item.name: Organizational AI readiness
item.description: An organization's preparedness across people, processes, and governance to adopt, scale, and govern AI, distinct from having AI tools or infrastructure.
item.grounding_span: Organizational AI readiness encourages executives and leaders to look beyond tools and infrastructure alone before proceeding with AI implementations.

item.name: AI adoption
item.description: Whether and how effectively, consistently, and ethically people actually use AI tools to deliver outcomes.
item.grounding_span: the success of AI initiatives depends far more on whether the organization’s people are prepared to adopt, trust, and use it than on the AI technologies themselves

item.name: Data, governance and privacy
item.description: Practices ensuring data accuracy, accessibility, security, and regulatory compliance as a foundation for AI readiness.
item.grounding_span: AI is only as effective as the data it relies on, making strong data governance and privacy practices foundational to readiness.

item.name: Data quality
item.description: The accuracy and reliability of underlying data, whose absence causes AI outputs to become unreliable.
item.grounding_span: Without this foundation, AI outputs become unreliable, and trust in AI technologies erodes.

item.name: Leadership vision and strategy
item.description: A clear vision from leadership defining priority use cases and aligning AI initiatives to business outcomes.
item.grounding_span: A clear, compelling vision from leadership sets the direction for how AI will create value across the organization.

item.name: Talent and skill development
item.description: A broad skills uplift including data literacy and specialized capabilities in data science, engineering, and AI governance.
item.grounding_span: AI readiness requires a broader skills uplift across the organization.

item.name: Technology capabilities and implementation approach
item.description: A robust, scalable technology ecosystem—infrastructure, data platforms, integration, and AI tools—supporting AI development and use.
item.grounding_span: A robust and scalable technology ecosystem is essential to support artificial intelligence development and deployment.

item.name: Cultural behaviors and mindset
item.description: Cultural attitudes toward AI; encouraging experimentation and data-driven decisions accelerates adoption while fear or distrust stalls it.
item.grounding_span: Organizational culture plays a decisive role in whether AI is embraced or resisted.

item.name: Distributed, cross-functional ownership
item.description: Shared ownership of AI across business, technology, risk, and operations functions.
item.grounding_span: AI readiness requires shared ownership across business, technology, risk, and operations functions.

item.name: Executive behavior
item.description: Leadership conduct that is described as one of the strongest predictors of whether AI initiatives stall or scale.
item.grounding_span: including executive behavior — one of the strongest predictors of whether AI initiatives stall or scale

item.name: Trust in AI
item.description: Confidence in AI tools, which varies by role, with executives reporting higher trust than frontline workers.
item.grounding_span: executives report higher trust (+1.09) and ease of use (+1.19) than frontline workers

item.name: Ease of use
item.description: Perceived usability of AI tools, which varies by role.
item.grounding_span: AI tools are often perceived as easy to use and valuable, yet adoption still varies by role

item.name: User proficiency
item.description: Users' skill in effectively using AI; cited as the most common AI adoption challenge.
item.grounding_span: the most common challenge is user proficiency (38%)

item.name: Human factors
item.description: The people-side elements—communication, training, leadership behavior, culture—that account for the majority of AI implementation difficulties.
item.grounding_span: human factors account for 56–64% of AI implementation difficulties

item.name: Change management
item.description: The discipline of transforming human behavior so that AI strategy and governance translate into employee adoption, proficiency, and sustained use.
item.grounding_span: Change management makes AI readiness real by turning AI strategy and governance into employee adoption, proficiency and sustained use, where the value is actually realized.

item.name: Governance and control
item.description: How clearly rules, guardrails, and decision rights are understood and experienced at different levels of the organization.
item.grounding_span: **Governance and control** – How clearly rules, guardrails, and decision rights are understood and experienced at different levels

item.name: AI implementation approach
item.description: Whether AI is perceived as strategic and coordinated versus reactive and ad hoc, and whether a level is involved in shaping use cases.
item.grounding_span: **AI implementation approach** – Whether people see AI as strategic and coordinated vs. reactive and ad hoc, and whether their level is involved in shaping use cases or just receiving tools

item.name: Organizational dynamics
item.description: Perception differences between levels in the organization.
item.grounding_span: **Organizational dynamics** – Perception differences between levels in the organization

item.name: Training and capability-building
item.description: Role-based education, coaching, and hands-on learning opportunities for building confidence to use AI effectively.
item.grounding_span: **Training and capability-building** – Gaps in role-based education, coaching, and hands-on learning opportunities for building confidence to use AI effectively

item.name: Role-based training
item.description: Training tailored by role, proficiency level, and use case, contrasted with one-size-fits-all tool training.
item.grounding_span: Expand AI literacy across the organization with role-based training that helps people understand both the opportunities and limitations of AI, not just how to use specific tools.

item.name: Readiness scorecard
item.description: The output of scoring segments across dimensions, covering both organizational and human factors, not just technology.
item.grounding_span: This gives you a readiness scorecard that covers both organizational and human factors, not just technology.

item.name: Readiness constraints
item.description: The most significant bottlenecks that limit adoption and value realization, such as low proficiency, lack of transparency, or unbalanced governance.
item.grounding_span: determine the two most significant bottlenecks that will limit adoption and value realization

item.name: Role/level segmentation
item.description: Breaking the organization into key groups by role or level so readiness differences by level become visible.
item.grounding_span: Break the organization into key groups, such as executives, people managers, team leaders, and frontline employees, so you can see where readiness differs by level.

item.name: Perception gaps between executives and frontline
item.description: Differences in trust and ease of use between executives and frontline employees that leaders may overlook.
item.grounding_span: executives typically report higher trust and ease of use with AI than frontline employees

item.name: Culture of experimentation
item.description: An environment with clear guardrails that leaves room to test and learn, enabling responsible AI innovation.
item.grounding_span: Clear guardrails with room to test and learn are essential to building confidence and enabling responsible AI innovation.

item.name: Responsible AI
item.description: Integrating responsible AI principles into training, decision criteria, and project reviews.
item.grounding_span: Make ethics a visible priority by integrating responsible AI principles into training, decision criteria, and project reviews.

item.name: AI roadmap
item.description: A simple, living roadmap outlining priority use cases, business outcomes, and key milestones.
item.grounding_span: building a simple, living AI roadmap that outlines priority use cases, business outcomes, and key milestones

item.name: Targeted interventions
item.description: Actions chosen to directly address top readiness constraints for the right segments, with owners and timing.
item.grounding_span: Choose actions that directly address those constraints for the right segments.

item.grounding_span: measures and indicators of nonsampling error are computed and documented

item.name: Nonresponse
item.description: A source of nonsampling error including household/establishment nonresponse, person nonresponse, and item nonresponse.
item.grounding_span: Nonresponse (e.g., bias from household/establishment nonresponse, person nonresponse, and item nonresponse).

item.name: Unit nonresponse
item.description: Failure of an entire sampled unit to respond, measured by unit response rates.
item.grounding_span: weighted response rates must be computed to measure unit and item nonresponse

item.name: Item nonresponse
item.description: Failure to obtain a response for a particular data item within an otherwise responding unit.
item.grounding_span: person nonresponse, and item nonresponse

item.name: Coverage error
item.description: A source of nonsampling error from listing error, duplicates, undercoverage, overcoverage, and frame/universe mismatches.
item.grounding_span: Coverage (e.g., listing error, duplicates, undercoverage, overcoverage, and mismatches between the frame of administrative records and the universe of interest for the information product).

item.name: Coverage ratio
item.description: An indicator of coverage error and potential bias computed using statistically sound methods.
item.grounding_span: Coverage ratios must be computed to measure coverage error, as an indicator of potential bias

item.name: Processing error
item.description: A source of nonsampling error from coding, data entry, editing, weighting, record linkage, disclosure avoidance, and assumption inaccuracies.
item.grounding_span: Processing (e.g., errors due to coding, data entry, editing, weighting, linking records, disclosure avoidance methods, and inaccuracies of assumptions used to develop estimates).

item.name: Measurement error
item.description: A source of nonsampling error from interviewer/respondent behavior, instrument design, collection modes, and inconsistent administrative data.
item.grounding_span: Measurement (e.g., errors due to interviewer and respondent behavior, data collection instrument design, data collection modes, definitions of reference periods, reporting unit definitions, and inconsistencies in administrative records data).

item.name: Nonresponse bias
item.description: Bias in estimates arising from nonresponse; triggers required analysis when response rates fall below thresholds.
item.grounding_span: Nonresponse bias analyses must be conducted when unit, item, or total quantity response rates for the total sample or important subpopulations fall below the following thresholds.

item.name: Weighted response rate
item.description: Response rate computed with weights accounting for selection probabilities including subsampling for nonresponse follow-up.
item.grounding_span: weighted response rates must be computed to measure unit and item nonresponse

item.name: Unweighted response rate
item.description: Response rate computed using unweighted data, permitted in specified situations such as monitoring collection or preserving time series.
item.grounding_span: Response rates may be computed using unweighted data when:

item.name: Unit response rate
item.description: Rate of responding units; nonresponse bias analysis is required below an 80 percent threshold.
item.grounding_span: The threshold for unit response rates is 80 percent.

item.name: Item response rate
item.description: Rate of response for key items; nonresponse bias analysis is required below a 70 percent threshold.
item.grounding_span: The threshold for item response rates of key items is 70 percent.

item.name: Item allocation/imputation rate
item.description: Rate at which key-variable items are allocated or imputed, computed for demographic surveys and censuses.
item.grounding_span: item response rates or item allocation/imputation rates (for key variables)

item.name: Total item response rate
item.description: Aggregate item response rate computed for demographic surveys and decennial censuses.
item.grounding_span: and total item response rates

item.name: Quantity response rate
item.description: Response rate for key variables in economic surveys and censuses.
item.grounding_span: quantity response rates (for key variables)

item.name: Total quantity response rate
item.description: Aggregate quantity-based response rate; nonresponse bias analysis is required below a 70 percent threshold.
item.grounding_span: The threshold for total quantity response rates is 70 percent.

item.name: Cumulative response rate
item.description: Weighted response rate reflecting total attrition of eligible units over repeated waves or successive stages of collection.
item.grounding_span: cumulative response rates must be computed using weighted data

item.name: Selection probabilities
item.description: Probabilities of sample selection, including subsampling for nonresponse follow-up, that weights must account for.
item.grounding_span: The weights must account for selection probabilities, including probabilities associated with subsampling for nonresponse follow-up.

item.name: Convenience sample
item.description: A non-randomly selected sample for which computing response rates is generally not appropriate.
item.grounding_span: convenience samples or samples with self-selected respondents

item.name: Equivalent quality data
item.description: Data of equivalent quality (e.g., administrative records, SEC filings, annual reports) used for nonresponding tabulation units in total quantity response rates.
item.grounding_span: the sources of equivalent quality data for nonresponding tabulation units must be listed

item.name: Key variables
item.description: The variables/items for which item, allocation, and quantity response rates are computed.
item.grounding_span: quantity response rates (for key variables)

item.name: Longitudinal/panel survey
item.description: A survey with repeated waves for which cumulative response rates reflecting attrition must be computed.
item.grounding_span: For panel or longitudinal surveys, cumulative response rates must be computed using weighted data

item.name: Administrative records
item.description: External record sources whose nonsampling error measures (coverage, missingness, edits, nonmatches) must be computed.
item.grounding_span: Measures or indicators of nonsampling error associated with data from administrative records must be computed to inform users of the quality of the data.

item.name: Nonresponse bias analysis
item.description: Required analysis of potential bias when response rates fall below defined thresholds.
item.grounding_span: Nonresponse bias analyses must be conducted

item.name: Reinterview
item.description: A response-error evaluation method used to generate measures of nonsampling error.
item.grounding_span: Response error evaluation studies (e.g., reinterview and latent class analysis).

item.name: Latent class analysis
item.description: An analytic method used in response-error evaluation studies.
item.grounding_span: reinterview and latent class analysis

item.name: Interviewer variance
item.description: Variance attributable to interviewers, assessed through interviewer variance studies.
item.grounding_span: Interviewer variance studies.

item.name: Respondent debriefing
item.description: A study method for assessing measurement error via debriefing of respondents.
item.grounding_span: Respondent debriefing studies.

item.name: Response analysis survey
item.description: A study that generates measures or indicators of nonsampling error.
item.grounding_span: Response analysis surveys.

item.name: Geocoding evaluation
item.description: Studies of address matching and geographic allocation rates that indicate nonsampling error.
item.grounding_span: Geocoding evaluation studies (e.g., address matching rates and analysis of rates of allocation to higher level geographic entities based on postal place-name or ZIP Code matches).

item.name: Mode effect
item.description: Effects of data collection mode on responses, assessed through mode effect studies.
item.grounding_span: Mode effect studies.

item.name: Data entry error rate
item.description: An indicator of processing nonsampling error for data entry/capture operations.
item.grounding_span: Error rates for data entry/data capture operations.

item.name: Coding error rate
item.description: Error and referral rates for coding operations as indicators of nonsampling error.
item.grounding_span: Error rates and referral rates for coding operations.

item.name: Imputation/edit change rate
item.description: Rates for editing and imputation operations that indicate nonsampling error.
item.grounding_span: Imputation rates and edit change rates for editing and imputation operations.

item.name: Disclosure avoidance
item.description: Disclosure avoidance methods, listed as a processing source of nonsampling error.
item.grounding_span: disclosure avoidance methods

item.name: Information product
item.description: Any product released by the Census Bureau to which the statistical quality standards apply.
item.grounding_span: all information products released by the Census Bureau

item.name: Quality control
item.description: Interviewer and processing quality control activities producing measures/indicators and driving improvements.
item.grounding_span: interviewer quality control (QC) results

item.name: Transparency
item.description: Providing users insight into data quality, a stated purpose of computing and documenting error measures.
item.grounding_span: to provide transparency regarding the quality of the data

item.name: Record linkage
item.description: Linking of records across data sets, a processing operation and error source (nonmatches, clerical linkage QC).
item.grounding_span: error rates from clerical coding and clerical record linkage

item.name: Confidentiality / protected information
item.description: Protection against unauthorized release of protected or administratively restricted information under federal law and Bureau policy.
item.grounding_span: unauthorized release of protected information or administratively restricted information must be prevented by following federal laws

item.claim_text: The purpose of this standard is to specify the documentation that must be readily accessible to the public to ensure transparency and reproducibility in information products released by the Census Bureau.
item.grounding_span: The purpose of this standard is to specify the documentation that must be readily accessible to the public to ensure transparency and reproducibility in information products released by the Census Bureau.

item.claim_text: Because federal law and Census Bureau policies require safeguarding confidentiality, complete transparency and reproducibility may not always be possible.
item.grounding_span: complete transparency and reproducibility may not always be possible

item.claim_text: At a minimum, the documentation will allow users to assess the accuracy and reliability of the estimates and results in the Census Bureau’s information products.
item.grounding_span: At a minimum, the documentation will allow users to assess the accuracy and reliability of the estimates and results in the Census Bureau’s information products.

item.claim_text: Documentation that would breach the confidentiality of protected or administratively restricted information, or violate data-use agreements with other agencies, must not be released.
item.grounding_span: Documentation that would breach the confidentiality of protected information or administratively restricted information or that would violate data-use agreements with other agencies must not be released.

item.claim_text: Documentation must be readily accessible in sufficient detail to allow qualified users to understand and analyze the information and to reproduce and evaluate the results.
item.grounding_span: Documentation must be readily accessible in sufficient detail to allow qualified users to understand and analyze the information and to reproduce (within the constraints of confidentiality requirements) and evaluate the results.

item.grounding_span: The Census Bureau’s statistical quality standards apply to all information products released by the Census Bureau and the activities that generate those products

item.name: Strategy
item.description: Readiness area concerned with alignment on direction and level of ambition; defining an AI vision and goals aligned to organizational objectives.
item.grounding_span: Strategy. Because AI is a transformative technology, alignment on direction and level of ambition is crucial.

item.name: People
item.description: Readiness area concerned with accessing, recruiting, and upskilling the technical and AI skills of the workforce.
item.grounding_span: People. Agencies may face challenges around accessing and recruiting necessary technical skills, as well as helping existing employees develop and deploy AI skills.

item.name: Processes
item.description: Readiness area concerned with establishing processes, controls, and governance systems and integrating AI into the work of the organization.

item.description: Readiness area concerned with data quality and a data governance system covering sourcing, accessing, and quality management.

item.name: AI capability
item.description: The basic types of things that AI can do; the unit of analysis for the OECD indicators.
item.grounding_span: we use the terms “capability” to refer to the basic types of things that AI can do and “ability” to refer to the basic types of things that humans can do.

item.name: Human ability
item.description: The basic types of things that humans can do; the reference baseline against which AI capabilities are compared.
item.grounding_span: “ability” to refer to the basic types of things that humans can do

item.name: OECD AI Capability Indicators
item.description: Nine indicators developed by the OECD to describe AI development across the full range of human abilities.
item.grounding_span: To show AI development across the full range of human abilities, the OECD has developed nine AI Capability Indicators

item.name: Five-level scale
item.description: Scale structure representing increasing difficulty of tasks for AI systems, with levels marked by qualitative differences rather than gradual improvement.
item.grounding_span: The OECD created scales with five levels to represent the increasing difficulty of tasks for AI systems
item.location: Chapter 2, Building scales with five levels

item.name: Level 1 (solved AI challenges)
item.description: The lowest scale level, reflecting AI challenges already solved, such as retrieval.
item.grounding_span: In each scale, level 1 reflects solved AI challenges (e.g. Google Search’s retrieval capabilities)
item.location: Chapter 2, Building scales with five levels

item.name: Level 5 (simulates all aspects of human ability)
item.description: The top scale level, representing performance that simulates all aspects of the corresponding human ability.
item.grounding_span: level 5 represents performance that simulates all aspects of the corresponding human abilities
item.location: Chapter 2, Building scales with five levels

item.name: Capability-based framework
item.description: The OECD's framing that shifts focus from fragmented tasks to core human abilities, grounded in human psychology.
item.grounding_span: The OECD instead adopts a capability-based framework, shifting focus from fragmented tasks to core human abilities

item.name: Task-based approach
item.description: Labour economics approach analysing AI's impact through the collections of tasks that make up occupations.
item.grounding_span: This task-based approach has been a major innovation in labour economics research

item.name: Occupation-based analysis
item.description: Earlier economics approach analysing AI's impact at the level of whole occupations, superseded by task-based analysis.
item.grounding_span: the economics literature has moved from occupation-based analyses of the impact of AI on work to analyses based on tasks

item.name: Artificial general intelligence
item.description: AI that matches the full range of human cognitive and social abilities.
item.grounding_span: artificial general intelligence (AGI), which is generally understood as AI that matches the full range of human cognitive and social abilities
item.location: Chapter 2, A framework for defining and measuring artificial general intelligence

item.name: Superhuman AGI
item.description: An AGI system characterised by DeepMind as outperforming all humans across all tasks.
item.grounding_span: Google DeepMind defined a superhuman AGI system as one that "outperforms 100% of humans" across all tasks
item.location: Chapter 2, A framework for defining and measuring artificial general intelligence

item.name: Qualitatively superhuman performance
item.description: Aspects of AI capability that go beyond the scope of human abilities entirely.
item.grounding_span: Future extensions of the scale may include aspects of AI capabilities that go beyond the scope of human abilities, which can be described as _qualitatively_ superhuman aspects of AI performance.
item.location: Chapter 2, Building scales with five levels

item.name: Quantitatively superhuman performance
item.description: AI outperforming humans on speed, accuracy or data coverage while doing things humans can also do.
item.grounding_span: AI simply outperforms humans on speed, or accuracy or data coverage but is otherwise doing things that humans can also do
item.location: Chapter 2, Building scales with five levels

item.name: Jagged frontier
item.description: Description of LLM capability development as advanced in some domains and limited in others.
item.grounding_span: The development of LLM capabilities has been described as a "jagged frontier"
item.location: Chapter 2, A framework for defining and measuring artificial general intelligence

item.name: Benchmark performance
item.description: Measurement of AI via standard benchmark tests; unclear to non-experts when taken in isolation and lacking a human baseline.
item.grounding_span: discuss capabilities purely in terms of benchmark performance without any comparison to human abilities
item.location: Chapter 2, AI has progressed beyond our understanding of its capabilities

item.name: Expert judgement
item.description: Judgement used to fill gaps where formal comparable tests of AI and human performance do not exist.
item.grounding_span: the OECD draws on whatever evidence is available and uses expert judgement to fill in the gaps
item.location: Chapter 2, Building scales with five levels

item.name: Structured peer review

item.name: Agentic AI
item.description: Artificial intelligence characterized by systems that autonomously execute end-to-end, multi-step workflows, described as a fundamental shift in capability.
item.grounding_span: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is driving a fundamental shift in capability, allowing systems to autonomously execute end-to-end, multi-step workflows.

item.name: Autonomous execution of end-to-end, multi-step workflows
item.description: The capability that distinguishes agentic AI: systems carrying out complete multi-step workflows without step-by-step human execution.
item.grounding_span: allowing systems to autonomously execute end-to-end, multi-step workflows

item.name: Fundamental shift in capability
item.description: The step-change in AI capability that agentic AI is said to be driving.
item.grounding_span: is driving a fundamental shift in capability

item.name: Government operations and citizen services
aliases: how governments operate and serve citizens
item.description: The domain of government activity — internal operations and service delivery to citizens — that agentic AI is expected to transform.
item.grounding_span: This technological progress is poised to transform how governments operate and serve citizens.

item.name: Public value
item.description: The benefit agentic AI can deliver in the public sector; the criterion used to decide where to deploy it.
item.grounding_span: where agentic AI can deliver the greatest public value

item.name: Strategic, evidence-based grasp of agentic AI opportunity
item.description: An informed, evidence-grounded understanding of where agentic AI delivers value, whose absence exposes governments to investment risk.
item.grounding_span: without a strategic, evidence-based grasp of where agentic AI can deliver the greatest public value

item.name: Balancing potential against complexity
item.description: The trade-off criterion for selecting agentic AI opportunities: high potential paired with complexity that can be managed.
item.grounding_span: balancing high potential with manageable complexity

item.name: Misallocated investment
item.description: The risk that governments direct agentic AI investment toward low-value or unsuitable areas.
item.grounding_span: governments risk investing in the wrong places

item.name: Confidence in the technology
item.description: Trust in agentic AI, which poorly targeted investment is said to undermine.
item.grounding_span: undermining confidence in the technology

item.name: Pilots that fail to scale
item.description: Agentic AI pilots launched in the public sector that do not progress to scaled deployment.
item.grounding_span: launching pilots that fail to scale

item.name: Department-agnostic perspective on government activities
item.description: An analytical lens that looks at government activities independently of departmental boundaries.
item.grounding_span: applies a novel, department‑agnostic perspective on government activities

item.name: Approach to assess agentic AI value and risk
item.description: The method the report provides for assessing where agentic AI delivers public value and which risks must be managed first.
item.grounding_span: It provides a clear approach to assess where agentic AI can deliver the greatest public value and what risks must be managed before deployment at scale.

item.name: Risks to be managed before scale deployment
item.description: Risks the report holds must be addressed prior to deploying agentic AI at scale.
item.grounding_span: what risks must be managed before deployment at scale

item.description: Full-scale operational rollout of agentic AI, as distinct from pilots.

item.name: Language capability
item.description: AI capability to understand, interpret and generate human language.

item.description: AI capability to produce valuable, novel and surprising outputs.
item.grounding_span: Creativity is often assumed to be exclusively human and outside the limits of AI
